structural_assumptions: Demand is the daily count of 311 service requests created (intake), not measured workload: one request is one unit of work, whatever its type or agency.

One city-wide pool: staff and capacity are fully interchangeable across the agencies and request types that the city-wide count mixes. A split by agency with the same total capacity can only leave as much backlog or more, so pooled backlogs are optimistic.
The repository holds no closures, backlog, staffing, service-level or cost data: every operational parameter, the initial backlog included, is HYPOTHETICAL.
Quantities are continuous (fractional requests and staff hours); arrivals can be served on the day they arrive; capacity not used on a day is lost.

Demand is treated as known when planning (a deterministic model of the M2 point forecast or of a labelled stress path), although the forecast's historical error is large and the M3 intervals failed their calibration criteria; no chance constraint and no probability of meeting any target is computed.
The penalised score adds HYPOTHETICAL notional penalty weights to discretionary cash. It ranks plans for one set of weights; it is not a cost and is never compared as one.
limitations: Every operational parameter is HYPOTHETICAL; ATLAS holds no staffing, productivity, cost, budget, backlog or capacity data for any NYC agency.

The demand is an unvalidated point forecast (or a labelled stress path), treated as known: the plan is optimal only for this demand path. The forecast's historical MAE over horizons 1-30 was 985 requests/day, 1.1 times this simulation's largest daily overtime capacity (900 requests/day).
Horizon totals are not prorated: overtime_total_hours keeps its 30-day reference value over this 7-day horizon.
No probability of meeting any target is computed or implied: the model is deterministic and the M3 status in integrity governs every interval.
One pooled city-wide unit with continuous quantities: the most favourable sharing assumption, without shifts, integer staff or fixed costs.
The penalised score mixes cash with notional weights; it ranks plans and is never a cost. Shadow prices are not computed for interactive simulations.
Nothing here is a validated staffing, budget or service-capacity recommendation.
